attempts.summary: Created a LUKS2-encrypted volume (aes-xts-plain64, file-backed at /root/secure.img, auto-unlocked via a root-only keyfile at /etc/luks-keys/secure.key) mounted at /srv/secure with an XFS filesystem on node1. Configured /etc/crypttab (systemd's native file-backed loop support) and /etc/fstab so the volume unlocks and mounts automatically on boot with no manual intervention or interactive passphrase. Verified across a full node reboot: boot identity changed (proving a real restart), systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service came up active automatically, /srv/secure was mounted from /dev/mapper/secure, and a test file written before the reboot was readable afterward, confirming both automatic unlock and data integrity.
